data.gender_notes: Balduin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Balduin is derived from the Germanic words ‘balde’ meaning bold or brave and ‘win’ meaning friend. This name was popular among the European nobility in the Middle Ages. It is a strong, masculine name with a rich history. The name Balduin carries the meaning “Brave friend” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Balduin usually hope their child will grow to embody brave friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and loyalty.
data.etymology: Balduin belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave friend.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balduin total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Balduin was borne by several medieval European rulers, including Baldwin I of Jerusalem, the founder of the County of Edessa and the Crusader Principality of Antioch; Baldwin II of Constantinople, who was the first Latin Emperor of Constantinople; and Baldwin IV of Flanders, who lived during the Crusades and was known for his bravery in battle. This name is associated with courage, power, and nobility, and was a mark of distinction among the European noble classes.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Balduin carries the spiritual meaning of a bold and brave friend of God. The name symbolizes courage in standing up for one's beliefs and values, as well as having the strength and courage to help others in times of need. It can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of having God as a constant companion and friend, and to live a life that reflects that friendship in courageous and noble ways.
